primary_diagnosis_treated: Diabetic nephropathy (CKD stage 4) with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, anemia
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.dose: 1.25 mg orally once daily; titrate to 2.5 mg after 2 weeks, then to 5 mg as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after each titration step
medications.purpose: Reduce intraglomerular pressure, slow CKD progression, control hypertension and proteinuria
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE‑I for CKD with ACR ≥ 30 mg/mmol or hypertension; monitor creatinine & potassium after 1–2 weeks

medications.duration: Lifelong — review lipid profile at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD (risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends statin for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.dose: 0.1 U/kg subcutaneously once daily (e.g., 5 U) – titrate to fasting glucose 4–7 mmol/L
medications.duration: Lifelong — review glucose logs every 3 months
medications.purpose: Glycaemic control in type 2 diabetes with eGFR < 20 mL/min/1.73 m² (oral agents unsafe)
medications.nice_justification: NICE diabetes guideline (NG28) recommends insulin when eGFR < 20 mL/min/1.73 m²

medications.dose: 4 U subcutaneously before each main meal – adjust according to post‑prandial glucose
medications.duration: Lifelong — review with basal insulin every 3 months
medications.purpose: Prandial glucose control as part of basal‑bolus regimen
medications.nice_justification: NICE diabetes guideline (NG28) for intensive insulin therapy when basal alone insufficient

medications.dose: 5 mg orally once daily; may increase to 10 mg if BP target not met
medications.duration: Lifelong — review blood pressure after 2 weeks of initiation and then quarterly
medications.purpose: Additional antihypertensive to achieve target <130/80 mmHg (ACR ≥ 70 mg/mmol)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 BP target <130/80 mmHg for CKD with significant proteinuria; CCB safe in advanced CKD

medications.dose: 50 IU/kg subcutaneously weekly (adjust to maintain Hb 10–11 g/dL)
medications.duration: Until hemoglobin >10 g/dL, then reassess every 3 months
medications.purpose: Treat anemia of chronic kidney disease after iron repletion
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ESA when Hb < 10 g/dL and iron stores are adequate

medications.dose: 1 g orally every 6 hours as needed (max 4 g/day)
medications.purpose: Pain relief for chronic low back/neck pain while avoiding NSAIDs
medications.nice_justification: NG203 contraindicates chronic NSAIDs in CKD; recommends safe alternatives

contraindications.reason: eGFR 10.5 mL/min/1.73 m² – NSAIDs accelerate CKD progression and increase potassium retention
eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m² – risk of lactic acidosis
Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury, especially with eGFR < 15
Nephrotoxic and requires dose adjustment; patient has advanced CKD
High risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy with eGFR < 30
contraindications.alternative: Use low‑osmolar contrast with hydration or non‑contrast imaging

assumptions_warnings: Current blood pressure reading not provided – assume target not met, hence addition of amlodipine.
Serum potassium and liver function tests not available – baseline tests required before starting ramipril and atorvastatin.
Hemoglobin and iron studies not provided – ESA (epoetin alfa) to be initiated only after confirming Hb < 10 g/dL and iron repletion.
Allergy status unknown – verify no ACE‑I, statin, or insulin hypersensitivity before prescribing.
Weight and BMI not supplied – insulin dosing may need adjustment based on actual body weight.
treatment_summary: Start low‑dose ramipril and titrate cautiously, add atorvastatin for CV protection, initiate basal‑bolus insulin for diabetes, add amlodipine if BP remains above <130/80 mmHg, consider epoetin alfa for anemia after confirming labs, and use paracetamol for pain while avoiding NSAIDs. All choices follow NICE NG203 (CKD) and relevant diabetes guidelines, with monitoring and safety checks outlined.
